universe.note: grew +2001 rows / +1 asset vs mission-start 2,590,975/3,585 due to external data ingestion

ratios_optimization.decision: reference regenerate_ratios RETAINED; indexed fast-path NOT adopted
ratios_optimization.why: fast path bins were byte-identical (0 bin cell diffs) but raw float values differed on 298/61,239 rows (sub-threshold; same bins) due to duplicate-timestamp pandas cov/reindex alignment, AND it was ~17% SLOWER (956s vs 817s) because the whole-df filter was never the dominant cost

adx_cross_slug_contamination.finding: gcp_dmv_osc.calculate_adx uses GLOBAL df.high.shift(1)/df.low.shift(1) for +DM/-DM (not per-slug shifts), so the first row of every slug is contaminated by the previous slug in the frame; ADX bins therefore depend on which other slugs share the frame
adx_cross_slug_contamination.implication: oscillators MUST be computed on the FULL universe frame in one pass; chunking them would change ADX values

execution_design.name: hybrid (full-frame osc + chunked per-slug remainder)
execution_design.why: monolithic full build needs ~31 GB peak (800 MB measured on 66k rows x 39.4x) — infeasible on this 15.7 GB machine; naive chunking is NOT byte-identical (ADX); hybrid is both
execution_design.mechanism: osc pass once on full frozen snapshot -> osc_bins.parquet; then chunk the per-slug-local families (momentum/tvv/ratios/var/metrics/scores), bitcoin benchmark loaded in every chunk, bitcoin output rows emitted once by chunk 0; idempotent upserts on (slug,date,methodology_version); resumable via chunk_progress
execution_design.equivalence: byte-identical to monolithic (hybrid_equivalence.json PASS: 21,326 rows, 0 cell diffs on 6-asset subset)
